title: Logo construction
slide_intent: Teach designers to preserve a symbol’s proportions and redraw its detail as display size changes. At a small size, too many dots can close the gaps that give the mark its form.
strategic_value: Halfkey can preserve the distinction between solid and dotted halves down to favicon scale by giving smaller masters fewer, larger dots.
demonstration: A circle and cell diagram defines the geometry at left. The center relates the lockup to its spacing unit. Four optical masters at right compare dot counts as the symbol grows.
practical_value: A designer can select a 16, 32, 64 or 128 px optical master for the output size and use the clear-space diagram to place the resulting lockup.

content_islands.name: Running header
content_islands.spec: Place the book identifiers at upper left and Logo construction with page 05 at upper right.

content_islands.name: Construction diagram
content_islands.spec: Place the split circle at left. Overlay a square grid on its dotted half, mark radius R and pitch p, and put the numbered construction rules below. Specify the inter-half gap as 0.075 R and cell pitch as R/5.

content_islands.name: Clear-space diagram
content_islands.spec: Center the horizontal lockup within its tinted clearance field. Use x for the symbol height, 0.4x for the wordmark gap and 0.5x for the surrounding clearance.

content_islands.name: Minimum sizes
content_islands.spec: Place separate Symbol, Lockup and Favicon entries below the clearance rules. Keep screen and print units attached to their values.

content_islands.name: Optical sizes
content_islands.spec: Stack the four masters down the right column with labels and use ranges. Show two, three, four and five dots across at the respective master sizes.
